The improved model represents tobacco BY-2 plant cells growing in stirred-tank bioreactors and consuming sucrose-derived sugars, ammonium, nitrate, and phosphate. It predicts cell dry mass and the concentrations of these nutrients and sugars over time, using an unstructured, segregated Monod-type description that distinguishes active and dead biomass and includes sucrose hydrolysis to glucose and fructose. The model represents the growth of Dunaliella viridis and its production of functional biomass, carbohydrates, neutral lipids, and chlorophyll as light and nitrogen conditions change. It predicts how carbon fixation and carbon allocation shift over time, using six dynamic state equations alongside calculations of light attenuation through the reactor. Its main mechanisms include light-limited, saturated, and inhibited photosynthesis; nitrogen-quota effects on carbon allocation; and distinct routes for lipid accumulation when nitrogen is sufficient or depleted.
